```{r}
#| label: setup
library(snpscaper)

x <- readRDS(params$data)
# Lists are passed in as comma-separated text, e.g. "2,3,4,5".
split_list <- function(text) strsplit(text, ",")[[1]]
k <- as.integer(split_list(params$k))
staff <- params$version == "staff"
set.seed(params$seed)

regions <- x$provenance$regions
genes <- teaching_genes[teaching_genes$gene %in% regions$label, ]
one_chromosome <- length(unique(x$variants$chrom)) == 1

# Data for each part of the report (see ?render_report)
common <- filter_snps(x, min_maf = params$min_maf)
pruned <- filter_snps(x, min_maf = params$min_maf, prune_ld = TRUE)

show_table <- function(df, ...) knitr::kable(df, format = "html", ...)
```

# The region

```{r}
#| label: tbl-regions
#| tbl-cap: "Region(s) analysed (GRCh38 coordinates)."
show_table(
  data.frame(
    Region = regions$label,
    Chromosome = regions$chrom,
    Start = format(regions$start, big.mark = ","),
    End = format(regions$end, big.mark = ","),
    `Length (kb)` = round((regions$end - regions$start + 1) / 1000, 1),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(genes))) {
  cat("**", genes$gene[i], "**: ", genes$description[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

The data come from the 1000 Genomes Project, which sequenced the genomes of
people from 26 populations, grouped into five continental super-populations:
African (AFR), Admixed American (AMR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR) and
South Asian (SAS).

# The data

```{r}
#| label: tbl-people
#| tbl-cap: "Number of people from each population included in this report."
people <- x$samples |>
  dplyr::count(super_pop, pop, pop_name, name = "People") |>
  dplyr::rename(`Super-population` = super_pop, Population = pop, `Population name` = pop_name)
show_table(people)
```

Each SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) is a position in the genome where
people carry different DNA letters (alleles). Only SNPs with exactly two
alleles are used. @tbl-steps shows how many SNPs remain after each
filtering step.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-steps
#| tbl-cap: "Number of SNPs after each processing step. MAF: minor allele frequency. LD pruning removes SNPs strongly correlated with a neighbour."
steps <- pruned$provenance$steps |>
  dplyr::rename(Step = step, People = people, SNPs = snps)
show_table(steps)
```

# Principal component analysis (PCA)

PCA summarises the differences between people's genotypes in a few
dimensions (principal components). People with similar genotypes appear
close together. The analysis uses `r ncol(pruned$genotypes)` LD-pruned SNPs.

```{r}
#| label: pca
pca_table <- suppressMessages(as_pca_table(pruned))
pca <- FactoMineR::PCA(pca_table, quali.sup = 1:3, graph = FALSE, ncp = 5)

plot_pca <- function(axes, colour_by, palette) {
  factoextra::fviz_pca_ind(
    pca,
    axes = axes,
    habillage = colour_by,
    palette = unname(palette[levels(pca_table[[colour_by]])]),
    geom = "point",
    pointshape = 19,
    pointsize = 1.2,
    alpha.ind = 0.7,
    mean.point = FALSE
  ) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = NULL) +
    theme_jb()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-superpop
#| fig-cap: "PCA: first and second principal components, coloured by super-population. Percentages give the share of variation captured by each component."
plot_pca(c(1, 2), "super_pop", superpop_colours)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-pop
#| fig-cap: "PCA: first and second principal components, coloured by population."
plot_pca(c(1, 2), "pop", pop_colours)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-13
#| fig-cap: "PCA: first and third principal components, coloured by super-population."
plot_pca(c(1, 3), "super_pop", superpop_colours)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-scree
#| fig-cap: "Share of the variation captured by each of the first ten principal components."
#| fig-height: 3.5
factoextra::fviz_eig(pca, ncp = 10, addlabels = TRUE, barfill = "grey60", barcolor = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = NULL) +
  theme_jb()
```

# Admixture analysis

Admixture analysis estimates, for each person, what proportion of their
genome comes from each of *K* ancestral groups. The groups are statistical
constructs, not real historical populations. *K* was varied from
`r min(k)` to `r max(k)`, with `r params$reps` runs for each *K*; the best
run is shown.

```{r}
#| label: admixture
adm <- run_admixture(pruned, k = k, reps = params$reps, seed = params$seed, verbose = FALSE)
best_k <- adm$cross_entropy$k[which.min(adm$cross_entropy$cross_entropy)]
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cross-entropy
#| fig-cap: "Cross-entropy for each K (grey: each run; black: best run). Lower values mean the model predicts left-out genotypes better."
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_cross_entropy(adm)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-admixture
#| fig-cap: "Estimated ancestry proportions for each person (thin vertical bars), grouped by super-population, for each K."
#| fig-height: !expr 1.4 + 1.3 * length(strsplit(params$k, ",")[[1]])
plot_admixture(adm, k = k, group = "super_pop")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-admixture-pop
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Estimated ancestry proportions grouped by population, for K = ", best_k, " (the K with the lowest cross-entropy).")
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_admixture(adm, k = best_k, group = "pop")
```

# Genetic differentiation (Fst)

Fst measures how much of the genetic variation lies between populations
rather than within them: 0 means identical allele frequencies, 1 means no
shared alleles. Calculated from `r ncol(common$genotypes)` SNPs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fst
#| fig-cap: "Pairwise Fst between populations."
#| fig-height: 7
plot_fst(calc_fst(common, by = "pop"), title = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fst
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise Fst between super-populations."
fst_super <- calc_fst(common, by = "super_pop")
if (nrow(fst_super) > 0) {
  show_table(
    dplyr::rename(fst_super, `Super-population 1` = group1, `Super-population 2` = group2, Fst = fst),
    digits = 3
  )
}
```

# Genetic diversity (heterozygosity)

Heterozygosity is the proportion of SNP genotypes at which a person carries
two different alleles. Expected heterozygosity is the value expected from
the population's allele frequencies if alleles paired at random.

```{r}
#| label: fig-het
#| fig-cap: "Expected (bars) and observed (points) heterozygosity in each population."
het <- calc_heterozygosity(common)
plot_heterozygosity(het, title = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-het
#| tbl-cap: "Heterozygosity in each population."
show_table(
  dplyr::rename(het, Population = pop, `Super-population` = super_pop, People = people, SNPs = snps, Observed = observed, Expected = expected),
  digits = 3
)
```

# Allele frequencies of key SNPs

```{r}
#| label: choose-snps
freqs <- calc_allele_freqs(x)
focal <- split_list(params$focal_snps)
focal_reason <- "chosen for this report"

if (length(focal) == 0) {
  focal <- teaching_snps$rsid[teaching_snps$gene %in% genes$gene]
  focal_reason <- "well-studied SNPs in this gene (see Notes for staff)"
}
if (length(focal) == 0) {
  # Otherwise, the SNP whose frequency differs most between super-populations
  spread <- calc_allele_freqs(common, by = "super_pop") |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(range = max(alt_freq) - min(alt_freq)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(range))
  focal <- spread$id[1]
  focal_reason <- "the SNP whose allele frequency differs most between super-populations"
}
focal <- focal[focal %in% c(freqs$id, freqs$rsid)]
```

SNPs shown here: `r if (length(focal) > 0) paste(focal, collapse = ", ") else "none found in these data"`
(`r focal_reason`). Allele names follow the reference genome: the
*reference* allele is the one in the human reference sequence, which is not
necessarily the ancestral or most common one.

```{r}
#| output: asis
for (i in seq_along(focal)) {
  chunk <- c(
    paste0("```{r}"),
    paste0("#| label: fig-freq-", i),
    paste0("#| fig-cap: 'Frequency of the alternative allele of ", focal[i], " in each population.'"),
    paste0("plot_freqs(freqs, '", focal[i], "')"),
    "```",
    "",
    paste0("```{r}"),
    paste0("#| label: fig-map-", i),
    paste0("#| fig-cap: 'Frequency of the alternative allele of ", focal[i], " on a world map.'"),
    "#| fig-height: 5.5",
    paste0("map_freqs(freqs, '", focal[i], "')"),
    "```",
    ""
  )
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = chunk, envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

# Linkage disequilibrium (LD)

Nearby SNPs tend to be inherited together. LD (measured as r²) shows how
strongly the genotypes at each pair of SNPs are correlated: from 0 (none) to
1 (complete). Each heatmap shows one super-population, using SNPs with a
minor allele frequency of at least 5% in that super-population.

```{r}
#| output: asis
if (!one_chromosome) {
  cat("LD heatmaps are only drawn for reports on a single chromosome.\n")
} else {
  for (group in intersect(names(superpop_colours), x$samples$super_pop)) {
    chunk <- c(
      "```{r}",
      paste0("#| label: fig-ld-", group),
      paste0("#| fig-cap: 'Linkage disequilibrium in the ", group, " super-population.'"),
      "#| fig-width: 6",
      "#| fig-height: 5.5",
      paste0("ld_data <- x |> keep_pops(super_pop = '", group, "') |> filter_snps(min_maf = 0.05)"),
      "if (ncol(ld_data$genotypes) >= 2) plot_ld(suppressMessages(calc_ld(ld_data, max_snps = 200)), title = NULL)",
      "```",
      ""
    )
    cat(knitr::knit_child(text = chunk, envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
  }
}
```

# Methods

Genotypes were obtained from the 1000 Genomes Project high-coverage phased
panel (GRCh38; Byrska-Bishop et al. 2022, *Cell* 185: 3426-3440), for the
`r format(nrow(x$samples), big.mark = ",")` people included, and fetched on
`r format(x$provenance$fetched, "%d %B %Y")`. Only biallelic SNPs were used.
SNPs with a minor allele frequency below `r params$min_maf` were removed. For
PCA and admixture analysis, SNPs were additionally pruned for linkage
disequilibrium (r² ≤ 0.2 within sliding windows of 50 SNPs).

PCA was performed with FactoMineR (Lê et al. 2008, *Journal of Statistical
Software* 25: 1-18) on scaled genotypes. Admixture analysis used the sNMF
algorithm of the LEA package (Frichot et al. 2014, *Genetics* 196: 973-983),
with `r params$reps` runs per *K* and random seed `r params$seed`. Fst was
estimated with Hudson's estimator combined across SNPs as a ratio of
averages (Bhatia et al. 2013, *Genome Research* 23: 1514-1521).

Report produced with snpscaper `r x$provenance$package_version`
(<https://github.com/jarekbryk/snpscaper>).

```{r}
#| output: asis
if (staff) {
  cat("# Notes for staff {.staff-notes}\n\n")
  if (nrow(genes) == 0) {
    cat("No curated notes are available for this region. Regions with no gene under strong selection usually show genome-wide patterns: the highest diversity in African populations, and Fst values that reflect continental groupings.\n")
  }
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(genes))) {
    cat("**", genes$gene[i], "**: ", genes$staff_notes[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
    snps <- teaching_snps[teaching_snps$gene == genes$gene[i], ]
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(snps))) {
      cat("- ", snps$rsid[j], ": ", snps$note[j], "\n", sep = "")
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
}
```
